card.intuition: Effort is a per-request dial controlling how much reasoning a model does before answering, from low (mechanical edits) to max (problems where a wrong answer is expensive). That thinking is generated at inference time like everything else and billed as output tokens even when the harness hides it. Set the dial to fit the task, not the session.
card.analogy: A code-review depth setting: skim for a formatting change, give a concurrency fix a full design review — you pay the reviewers for every minute either way, whether or not you see their notes.
card.time_complexity: Reasoning tokens are produced one at a time, so higher effort lengthens latency and raises the output-token bill even when the hidden thinking is never shown to you.
card.space_complexity: Thinking tokens occupy the same output side of the context as the visible answer, consuming token budget and time before the response you see even starts.
when_to_use: Turning effort up for tricky bugs, design decisions, and multi-step plans
Turning it low for mechanical edits, lookups, and well-specified changes with one clear path
Matching the dial to the task rather than the whole session
Dialing to max only for the hardest problems where a wrong answer is expensive to unwind
gotchas: Too-low effort on a hard problem yields a confident, shallow answer that reads fine and costs you later
Max effort on a one-line rename produces a long think the lowest setting would have skipped
Hidden reasoning is real work you're billed for, even though you never see it

steps.label: Low
steps.annotation: Mechanical edits and lookups get a one-clear-path answer.

steps.label: Medium
steps.annotation: Everyday coding is the usual default.

steps.label: High
steps.annotation: Tricky bugs and design decisions get longer deliberation.

steps.label: Max
steps.annotation: The hardest problems, where a wrong answer is expensive, get maximum thinking.

steps.label: Bill
steps.annotation: All of that reasoning is billed as output tokens even when hidden.

exercise.prompt: Model the effort ladder: given an effort level and the visible output, compute total billed output tokens as hidden thinking seconds plus shown output.
hints: Unknown levels should add zero hidden thinking
Use a dictionary lookup that defaults gracefully for missing keys

assert billed_output("max", 1) == 61
